-- | This is Hermod's core package and API for development of simple and
--   efficient tracers around the arrow based contra-tracer package
@package hermod-tracing-core
@version 1.0.0

module Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser

-- | The configuration source that should be ingested
data ConfigSource
FromFile :: FilePath -> ConfigSource
FromJSONObject :: Object -> ConfigSource
FromLazyBytes :: ByteString -> ConfigSource
FromStrictBytes :: ByteString -> ConfigSource

-- | Creates the minimal viable configuration by only setting fallback
--   values in an empty TraceConfig. Fallback options for the namespace
--   root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout logging. Notice
--   severity was chosen as it will never filter out any actionable traces
--   while creating minimal noise in the log.
mkConfiguration :: TraceConfig

-- | Creates the minimal viable configuration by only setting custom
--   fallback values in an empty TraceConfig. Fallback options for the
--   namespace root: custom values.
mkConfigurationWithFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   Fallback options for the namespace root: Notice severity, normal
--   detail, JSON stdout logging.
readConfiguration :: ConfigSource -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   Fallback options for the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> ConfigSource -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration file and return the internal representation. This
--   will silently provide a minimal viable config via
--   <tt>mkConfiguration</tt> when the file is absent. Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout
--   logging.
readConfiguration' :: FilePath -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration file and return the internal representation. This
--   will silently provide a minimal viable config via
--   <tt>mkConfigurationWithFallback</tt> when the file is absent. Fallback
--   options for the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallback' :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> FilePath -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   TraceConfig fields not specified in the file will be taken from the
--   provided <tt>defaultConf</tt> (when given there). Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout
--   logging.
readConfigurationWithDefault :: ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   TraceConfig fields not specified in the file will be taken from the
--   provided <tt>defaultConf</tt> (when given there). Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallbackAndDefault :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Applies the fallback values to the namespace root, or creates a
--   namespace root from them if none is present. Furthermore, it ensures a
--   metric prefix is properly namespaced, if there is one configured. If
--   you do not use any of mkConfiguration* or readConfiguration* to create
--   your TraceConfig, but do it manually, it is highly recommended to call
--   <tt>applyFallback</tt> on that TraceConfig value as a last step before
--   using it.
applyFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> TraceConfig -> TraceConfig

-- | Convert config from internal to external representation
configToRepresentation :: TraceConfig -> ConfigRepresentation
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigSource
instance GHC.Show.Show Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigSource
instance GHC.Show.Show Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigOptionRep
instance GHC.Show.Show Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigRepresentation
instance Data.Aeson.Types.FromJSON.FromJSON Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ExternalFile
instance Data.Aeson.Types.FromJSON.FromJSON Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigRepresentation
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigRepresentation
instance Data.Aeson.Types.FromJSON.FromJSON Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigOptionRep
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Hermod.Tracing.ConfigurationParser.ConfigOptionRep
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Hermod.Tracing.Types.Config.TraceConfig

module Hermod.Tracing.Consistency

-- | Warnings as a list of text
type NSWarnings = [Text]

-- | Checks if all namespaces in this configuration are legal. Legal in
--   this case means that it can be found by a hierarchical lookup in all
--   namespaces. Warns if namespaces in all namespaces are not unique,
--   Warns if namespaces in all namespaces are ending in the middle of
--   another namespace. The namespaces in allNamespaces are consistent with
--   the namespaces for the severityFor, privacyFor, detailsFor,
--   documentFor and metricsDocFor functions.
checkTraceConfiguration :: ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> [([Text], [Text])] -> IO NSWarnings
checkTraceConfiguration' :: TraceConfig -> [([Text], [Text])] -> NSWarnings
instance GHC.Show.Show Hermod.Tracing.Consistency.NSLookup

module Hermod.Tracing.Trace.Annotations
filterTraceBySeverity :: Monad m => Maybe SeverityF -> Trace m a -> Trace m a
filterTraceByPrivacy :: Monad m => Maybe Privacy -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set a fixed <a>SeverityS</a> on every message (no-op if already set).
setSeverity :: Monad m => SeverityS -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set severity from the <a>MetaTrace</a> instance for each message.
withSeverity :: forall m a. (Monad m, MetaTrace a) => Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set <a>Confidential</a> privacy on every message.
privately :: Monad m => Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set a fixed <a>Privacy</a> on every message (no-op if already set).
setPrivacy :: Monad m => Privacy -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set privacy from the <a>MetaTrace</a> instance for each message.
withPrivacy :: forall m a. (Monad m, MetaTrace a) => Trace m a -> Trace m a
allPublic :: a -> Privacy
allConfidential :: a -> Privacy

-- | Set a fixed <a>DetailLevel</a> on every message (no-op if already
--   set).
setDetails :: Monad m => DetailLevel -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set detail level from the <a>MetaTrace</a> instance for each message.
withDetails :: forall m a. (Monad m, MetaTrace a) => Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set prefix and inner namespace from the <a>MetaTrace</a> instance for
--   each message, prepending the given prefix names.
withNames :: forall m a. (Monad m, MetaTrace a) => [Text] -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Prepend a single name to the namespace prefix.
appendPrefixName :: Monad m => Text -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Prepend several names to the namespace prefix.
appendPrefixNames :: Monad m => [Text] -> Trace m a -> Trace m a
appendInnerName :: Monad m => Text -> Trace m a -> Trace m a
appendInnerNames :: Monad m => [Text] -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Set inner namespace from the <a>MetaTrace</a> instance for each
--   message.
withInnerNames :: forall m a. (Monad m, MetaTrace a) => Trace m a -> Trace m a

-- | Replace the logging context for all messages passing through this
--   trace.
withLoggingContext :: Monad m => LoggingContext -> Trace m a -> Trace m a

module Hermod.Tracing.Tracer.DataPoint

-- | Type wrapper for some value of type <tt>v</tt>. The only reason we
--   need this wrapper is an ability to store different values in the same
--   <a>DataPointStore</a>.
--   
--   Please note that when the acceptor application will read the value of
--   type <tt>v</tt> from the store, this value is just as unstructured
--   JSON, but not Haskell value of type <tt>v</tt>. That's why
--   <a>FromJSON</a> instance for type <tt>v</tt> should be available for
--   the acceptor application, to decode unstructured JSON.
data DataPoint
[DataPoint] :: (ToJSON v, NFData v) => !v -> DataPoint
type DataPointName = Text
type DataPointStore = TVar (Map DataPointName DataPoint)
initDataPointStore :: IO DataPointStore

-- | Write <a>DataPoint</a> to the store.
writeToStore :: DataPointStore -> DataPointName -> DataPoint -> IO ()
dataPointTracer :: forall m. MonadIO m => DataPointStore -> Trace m DataPoint
mkDataPointTracer :: forall dp. (ToJSON dp, MetaTrace dp, NFData dp) => Trace IO DataPoint -> IO (Trace IO dp)

--   gives the names of all tracers

module Hermod.Tracing.FrequencyLimiter

-- | Limits the frequency of messages to nMsg which is given per minute.
--   
--   If the limiter detects more messages, it traces randomly selected
--   messages with the given frequency on the <tt>vtracer</tt> until the
--   frequency falls under the threshold long enough.(see below)
--   
--   Before this the <tt>ltracer</tt> gets a <a>StartLimiting</a> message.
--   In-between you receive <tt>ContinueLimiting</tt> messages on the
--   <tt>ltracer</tt> every <a>reminderPeriod</a> seconds, with the number
--   of suppressed messages. Finally it sends a <a>StopLimiting</a> message
--   on the <tt>ltracer</tt> and traces all messages on the
--   <tt>vtracer</tt> again.
--   
--   A budget is used to decide when to start limiting and stop limiting,
--   so that the limiter does not get activated if few messages are send in
--   high frequency, and doesn't get deactivated if their are only few
--   messages which come with low frequency. When messages arrive in
--   shorter frequency then by the given <tt>thresholdFrequency</tt> budget
--   is earned, and if they arrive in a longer period budget is spend. If
--   budget is gets higher then <a>budgetLimit</a>, the limiter starts, and
--   if it falls below minus <a>budgetLimit</a> the limiter stops.
limitFrequency :: forall a m. MonadUnliftIO m => Double -> Text -> Trace m HermodTracingMessage -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)
data LimiterSpec
LimiterSpec :: [Text] -> Text -> Double -> LimiterSpec
[lsNs] :: LimiterSpec -> [Text]
[lsName] :: LimiterSpec -> Text
[lsFrequency] :: LimiterSpec -> Double
instance (GHC.Show.Show a, GHC.Show.Show b) => GHC.Show.Show (Hermod.Tracing.FrequencyLimiter.MaybeTuple' a b)
instance GHC.Show.Show a => GHC.Show.Show (Hermod.Tracing.FrequencyLimiter.FrequencyRec a)

module Hermod.Tracing.Configuration
data () => ConfigReflection
ConfigReflection :: IORef (Set [Text]) -> IORef (Set [Text]) -> IORef (Set [Text]) -> ConfigReflection
[crSilent] :: ConfigReflection -> IORef (Set [Text])
[crNoMetrics] :: ConfigReflection -> IORef (Set [Text])
[crAllTracers] :: ConfigReflection -> IORef (Set [Text])
data HermodException
HermodConfigException :: String -> HermodException
[excMessage] :: HermodException -> String
emptyConfigReflection :: IO ConfigReflection

-- | Call this function at initialisation, and later for reconfiguration.
--   Config reflection is used to optimise the tracers and has to collect
--   information about the tracers. Although it is possible to give more
--   then one tracer of the same time, it is not a common case to do this.
configureTracers :: forall a m. (MetaTrace a, MonadIO m) => ConfigReflection -> TraceConfig -> [Trace m a] -> m ()

-- | Take a selector function called <tt>extract</tt>. Take a function from
--   trace to trace with this config dependent value. In this way construct
--   a trace transformer with a config value
withNamespaceConfig :: forall m a b c. (MonadIO m, Ord b) => String -> (TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> m b) -> (Maybe b -> Trace m c -> Trace m a) -> Trace m c -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Filter a trace by severity and take the filter value from the config
filterSeverityFromConfig :: MonadIO m => Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Set detail level of a trace from the config
withDetailsFromConfig :: MonadIO m => Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Routing and formatting of a trace from the config
withBackendsFromConfig :: MonadIO m => (Maybe [BackendConfig] -> Trace m FormattedMessage -> Trace m a) -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Routing and formatting of a trace from the config
withLimitersFromConfig :: forall a m. MonadUnliftIO m => Trace m HermodTracingMessage -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Switch off any message of a particular tracer based on the
--   configuration. If the top tracer is silent and no subtracer is not
--   silent, then switch it off
maybeSilent :: forall m a. MonadIO m => (TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool) -> [Text] -> Bool -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)
isSilentTracer :: forall a. MetaTrace a => TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool
hasNoMetrics :: forall a. MetaTrace a => TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool

-- | By guaranteeing fallback values in the config's namespace root, the
--   Debug severity value here should never get used. If it has to be used,
--   this points to a severely erroneous config, or an implementation error
--   in the application's MetaTrace instance(s). For those cases only, this
--   ensures the affected trace message isn't silently filtered out.
getSeverity :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> SeverityF

-- | If no details can be found in the config, it is set to DNormal
getDetails :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> DetailLevel

-- | If no backends can be found in the config, it is set to [EKGBackend,
--   Forwarder, Stdout HumanFormatColoured]
getBackends :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> [BackendConfig]

module Hermod.Tracing.Tracer.Composed

-- | Construct a hermod tracer. The tracer gets a <tt>name</tt>, which is
--   appended to its namespace. The tracer has to be an instance of
--   LogFormatting for the display of messages and an instance of MetaTrace
--   for meta information such as severity, privacy, details and backends'.
--   The tracer gets the backends': <tt>trStdout</tt>, <tt>trForward</tt>
--   and <tt>mbTrEkg</tt> as arguments. The returned tracer needs to be
--   configured with a configuration before it is used.
mkHermodTracer :: forall evt. (LogFormatting evt, MetaTrace evt) => Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Maybe (Trace IO FormattedMessage) -> [Text] -> IO (Trace IO evt)

-- | Adds the possibility to add special tracers via the hook function
mkHermodTracer' :: forall evt evt1. (LogFormatting evt1, MetaTrace evt1) => Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Maybe (Trace IO FormattedMessage) -> [Text] -> (Trace IO evt1 -> IO (Trace IO evt)) -> IO (Trace IO evt)
mkMetricsTracer :: Maybe (Trace IO FormattedMessage) -> Trace IO FormattedMessage
traceTracerInfo :: Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Trace IO FormattedMessage -> ConfigReflection -> IO ()
traceConfigWarnings :: Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Trace IO FormattedMessage -> [Text] -> IO ()
traceEffectiveConfiguration :: Trace IO FormattedMessage -> Trace IO FormattedMessage -> TraceConfig -> IO ()


-- | Batteries-included public interface for the Hermod tracing system.
--   
--   A typical application wires up tracing in three steps:
--   
--   <ol>
--   <li><b>Define trace types</b>: for each domain-specific message type,
--   write <a>LogFormatting</a> (human/machine rendering, metrics) and
--   <a>MetaTrace</a> (namespace, severity, documentation) instances.</li>
--   <li><b>Construct backends</b>: call <a>mkHermodTracer</a> (or
--   <a>mkHermodTracer'</a>) with <a>standardTracer</a>, <a>ekgTracer</a>,
--   and/or <a>forwardTracer</a> to build a 'Trace IO YourType'.</li>
--   <li><b>Configure</b>: load a <a>TraceConfig</a> with
--   <a>readConfiguration</a> and apply it with <a>configureTracers</a>.
--   Use <a>checkTraceConfiguration</a> to validate the config against all
--   known namespaces at startup.</li>
--   </ol>
module Hermod.Tracing

-- | The class of contravariant functors.
--   
--   Whereas in Haskell, one can think of a <a>Functor</a> as containing or
--   producing values, a contravariant functor is a functor that can be
--   thought of as <i>consuming</i> values.
--   
--   As an example, consider the type of predicate functions <tt>a -&gt;
--   Bool</tt>. One such predicate might be <tt>negative x = x &lt; 0</tt>,
--   which classifies integers as to whether they are negative. However,
--   given this predicate, we can re-use it in other situations, providing
--   we have a way to map values <i>to</i> integers. For instance, we can
--   use the <tt>negative</tt> predicate on a person's bank balance to work
--   out if they are currently overdrawn:
--   
--   <pre>
--   newtype Predicate a = Predicate { getPredicate :: a -&gt; Bool }
--   
--   instance Contravariant Predicate where
--     contramap :: (a' -&gt; a) -&gt; (Predicate a -&gt; Predicate a')
--     contramap f (Predicate p) = Predicate (p . f)
--                                            |   `- First, map the input...
--                                            `----- then apply the predicate.
--   
--   overdrawn :: Predicate Person
--   overdrawn = contramap personBankBalance negative
--   </pre>
--   
--   Any instance should be subject to the following laws:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><i>Identity</i> <tt><a>contramap</a> <a>id</a> =
--   <a>id</a></tt></li>
--   <li><i>Composition</i> <tt><a>contramap</a> (g . f) = <a>contramap</a>
--   f . <a>contramap</a> g</tt></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   Note, that the second law follows from the free theorem of the type of
--   <a>contramap</a> and the first law, so you need only check that the
--   former condition holds.
class () => Contravariant (f :: Type -> Type)
contramap :: Contravariant f => (a' -> a) -> f a -> f a'

-- | Replace all locations in the output with the same value. The default
--   definition is <tt><a>contramap</a> . <a>const</a></tt>, but this may
--   be overridden with a more efficient version.
(>$) :: Contravariant f => b -> f b -> f a
infixl 4 >$
newtype () => Trace (m :: Type -> Type) a
Trace :: Tracer m (LoggingContext, Either TraceControl a) -> Trace (m :: Type -> Type) a
[unpackTrace] :: Trace (m :: Type -> Type) a -> Tracer m (LoggingContext, Either TraceControl a)

-- | Type wrapper for some value of type <tt>v</tt>. The only reason we
--   need this wrapper is an ability to store different values in the same
--   <a>DataPointStore</a>.
--   
--   Please note that when the acceptor application will read the value of
--   type <tt>v</tt> from the store, this value is just as unstructured
--   JSON, but not Haskell value of type <tt>v</tt>. That's why
--   <a>FromJSON</a> instance for type <tt>v</tt> should be available for
--   the acceptor application, to decode unstructured JSON.
data DataPoint
[DataPoint] :: (ToJSON v, NFData v) => !v -> DataPoint

-- | Call this function at initialisation, and later for reconfiguration.
--   Config reflection is used to optimise the tracers and has to collect
--   information about the tracers. Although it is possible to give more
--   then one tracer of the same time, it is not a common case to do this.
configureTracers :: forall a m. (MetaTrace a, MonadIO m) => ConfigReflection -> TraceConfig -> [Trace m a] -> m ()

--   trace to trace with this config dependent value. In this way construct
--   a trace transformer with a config value
withNamespaceConfig :: forall m a b c. (MonadIO m, Ord b) => String -> (TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> m b) -> (Maybe b -> Trace m c -> Trace m a) -> Trace m c -> m (Trace m a)

withLimitersFromConfig :: forall a m. MonadUnliftIO m => Trace m HermodTracingMessage -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Switch off any message of a particular tracer based on the
--   configuration. If the top tracer is silent and no subtracer is not
--   silent, then switch it off
maybeSilent :: forall m a. MonadIO m => (TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool) -> [Text] -> Bool -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)
isSilentTracer :: forall a. MetaTrace a => TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool
hasNoMetrics :: forall a. MetaTrace a => TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> Bool

-- | By guaranteeing fallback values in the config's namespace root, the
--   Debug severity value here should never get used. If it has to be used,
--   this points to a severely erroneous config, or an implementation error
--   in the application's MetaTrace instance(s). For those cases only, this
--   ensures the affected trace message isn't silently filtered out.
getSeverity :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> SeverityF

-- | If no details can be found in the config, it is set to DNormal
getDetails :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> DetailLevel

-- | If no backends can be found in the config, it is set to [EKGBackend,
--   Forwarder, Stdout HumanFormatColoured]
getBackends :: TraceConfig -> Namespace a -> [BackendConfig]

-- | Limits the frequency of messages to nMsg which is given per minute.
--   
--   If the limiter detects more messages, it traces randomly selected
--   messages with the given frequency on the <tt>vtracer</tt> until the
--   frequency falls under the threshold long enough.(see below)
--   
--   Before this the <tt>ltracer</tt> gets a <a>StartLimiting</a> message.
--   In-between you receive <tt>ContinueLimiting</tt> messages on the
--   <tt>ltracer</tt> every <a>reminderPeriod</a> seconds, with the number
--   of suppressed messages. Finally it sends a <a>StopLimiting</a> message
--   on the <tt>ltracer</tt> and traces all messages on the
--   <tt>vtracer</tt> again.
--   
--   A budget is used to decide when to start limiting and stop limiting,
--   so that the limiter does not get activated if few messages are send in
--   high frequency, and doesn't get deactivated if their are only few
--   messages which come with low frequency. When messages arrive in
--   shorter frequency then by the given <tt>thresholdFrequency</tt> budget
--   is earned, and if they arrive in a longer period budget is spend. If
--   budget is gets higher then <a>budgetLimit</a>, the limiter starts, and
--   if it falls below minus <a>budgetLimit</a> the limiter stops.
limitFrequency :: forall a m. MonadUnliftIO m => Double -> Text -> Trace m HermodTracingMessage -> Trace m a -> m (Trace m a)

-- | Creates the minimal viable configuration by only setting fallback
--   values in an empty TraceConfig. Fallback options for the namespace
--   root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout logging. Notice
--   severity was chosen as it will never filter out any actionable traces
--   while creating minimal noise in the log.
mkConfiguration :: TraceConfig

-- | Creates the minimal viable configuration by only setting custom
--   fallback values in an empty TraceConfig. Fallback options for the
--   namespace root: custom values.
mkConfigurationWithFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   Fallback options for the namespace root: Notice severity, normal
--   detail, JSON stdout logging.
readConfiguration :: ConfigSource -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   Fallback options for the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> ConfigSource -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration file and return the internal representation. This
--   will silently provide a minimal viable config via
--   <tt>mkConfiguration</tt> when the file is absent. Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout
--   logging.
readConfiguration' :: FilePath -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration file and return the internal representation. This
--   will silently provide a minimal viable config via
--   <tt>mkConfigurationWithFallback</tt> when the file is absent. Fallback
--   options for the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallback' :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> FilePath -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   TraceConfig fields not specified in the file will be taken from the
--   provided <tt>defaultConf</tt> (when given there). Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: Notice severity, normal detail, JSON stdout
--   logging.
readConfigurationWithDefault :: ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Read a configuration source and return the internal representation.
--   TraceConfig fields not specified in the file will be taken from the
--   provided <tt>defaultConf</tt> (when given there). Fallback options for
--   the namespace root: custom values.
readConfigurationWithFallbackAndDefault :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> IO TraceConfig

-- | Applies the fallback values to the namespace root, or creates a
--   namespace root from them if none is present. Furthermore, it ensures a
--   metric prefix is properly namespaced, if there is one configured. If
--   you do not use any of mkConfiguration* or readConfiguration* to create
--   your TraceConfig, but do it manually, it is highly recommended to call
--   <tt>applyFallback</tt> on that TraceConfig value as a last step before
--   using it.
applyFallback :: SeverityS -> DetailLevel -> BackendConfig -> TraceConfig -> TraceConfig

-- | Convert config from internal to external representation
configToRepresentation :: TraceConfig -> ConfigRepresentation

-- | Checks if all namespaces in this configuration are legal. Legal in
--   this case means that it can be found by a hierarchical lookup in all
--   namespaces. Warns if namespaces in all namespaces are not unique,
--   Warns if namespaces in all namespaces are ending in the middle of
--   another namespace. The namespaces in allNamespaces are consistent with
--   the namespaces for the severityFor, privacyFor, detailsFor,
--   documentFor and metricsDocFor functions.
checkTraceConfiguration :: ConfigSource -> TraceConfig -> [([Text], [Text])] -> IO NSWarnings
checkTraceConfiguration' :: TraceConfig -> [([Text], [Text])] -> NSWarnings

-- | Construct a hermod tracer. The tracer gets a <tt>name</tt>, which is
--   appended to its namespace. The tracer has to be an instance of
--   LogFormatting for the display of messages and an instance of MetaTrace
--   for meta information such as severity, privacy, details and backends'.
--   The tracer gets the backends': <tt>trStdout</tt>, <tt>trForward</tt>

--   configured with a configuration before it is used.
